closest_operator: conditional neural process with a graph edit input representation
missing_specific_reference: The phrase grammar-guided local data did not uniquely identify a primary paper despite targeted searches. No novelty credit is assigned to constrained perturbation generation.

sources.name: PGExplainer
sources.predictor_access: Frozen GNN embeddings and predictions; differentiable mask training.
sources.explainer_inputs: Endpoint embeddings and input graph; target-node embedding for node tasks.
sources.training_target: Prediction fidelity with size and entropy regularization.
sources.learned_component: Shared network parameterizing Concrete/Bernoulli edge masks.
sources.generalization: Across graph/node instances for a target predictor, not a query-conditioned held-out-function protocol.
sources.inference_cost: Embedding computation plus edge-network forward pass and selection.
sources.assumptions: Meaningful masking and fidelity criterion; neither chemical edit validity nor causal mechanism follows.
sources.remaining_difference: Signed complete-input edit responses and conditioning on another predictor transcript differ in task, not proof of a new amortization operator.
sources.code_status: Pinned TensorFlow codes/forgraph/Explainer.py: call and loss inspected.

sources.name: FastSHAP
sources.estimand: Shapley feature attributions for a specified missing-feature game.
sources.predictor_access: Value queries through a predictor/imputer; predictor gradients not required by the game.
sources.training_target: Shapley-kernel weighted coalition reconstruction, with efficiency normalization.
sources.learned_component: Amortized attribution network; a missing-feature surrogate may also be trained.
sources.generalization: Many instances of the explained task.
sources.inference_cost: One explainer forward pass online; imputer and explainer training cost upfront.
sources.assumptions: Feature-removal convention and sufficient function approximation.
sources.remaining_difference: A reference edit finite difference is not a Shapley value; direct signed-response reconstruction must be compared on its own endpoint.
sources.code_status: Pinned fastshap/fastshap.py: normalization, coalition reconstruction and validation inspected; primary HTML read.

sources.name: Stochastic amortization
sources.estimand: Approximate feature or data attributions otherwise costly to compute.
sources.predictor_access: Noisy attribution targets generated by the underlying attribution algorithm.
sources.explainer_inputs: Instance features and noisy targets during training.
sources.generalization: Across attribution instances in the trained task family.
sources.inference_cost: One forward pass after target generation and fitting.
sources.assumptions: Noise properties and conditional expectation determine the learned target; cheap noisy labels are not automatically unbiased.
sources.remaining_difference: Teacher-query amortization and noisy-target regression are established; neither is a distinct contribution here.

sources.name: GraphSHAP-IQ
sources.estimand: Any-order node-game Shapley interactions via sparse Moebius structure.
sources.predictor_access: GNN receptive fields and value queries; architecture-aware.
sources.explainer_inputs: Graph, masking game, message-passing depth and neighborhoods.
sources.training_target: No new explainer training target for exact computation.
sources.generalization: Per graph under its architectural assumptions.
sources.inference_cost: Coalition enumeration within receptive fields and Moebius transforms; exponential in local receptive-field size.
sources.assumptions: Linear global pooling and output layer for the stated exactness. Section 5 shows nonlinear readouts create nonlocal interactions.
sources.remaining_difference: Nonlinear graph edits fall outside the exactness theorem; that exclusion does not establish this proposal is novel or efficient.
sources.code_status: Pinned shapiq/explainer/graph/graphshapiq.py inspected; full paper including nonlinear-readout discussion read.

sources.name: SPEX
sources.estimand: Sparse Fourier representation of a binary masking value function, convertible to interaction attributions.
sources.explainer_inputs: Feature mask space and queried outputs.
sources.training_target: Sparse recovery from coded measurements; direct LASSO is an explicit alternative.
sources.inference_cost: Coded model queries plus sparse Fourier/channel decoding; configurations determine actual wall cost.
sources.assumptions: Sparse, low-order interactions and a valid binary product domain.
sources.remaining_difference: Applicable to a fully valid binary edit cube as a response reconstruction control. Eight states favor direct enumeration.
sources.code_status: Pinned spectralexplain/explainer.py plus paper algorithm/complexity read.

sources.name: ProxySPEX
sources.estimand: Reconstruct masked model outputs and recover influential sparse interactions.
sources.training_target: Fit gradient-boosted trees to queried values, then extract interactions.
sources.generalization: Across new instances by refitting; not free held-out-model adaptation.
sources.inference_cost: Queries, tree fitting and interaction extraction; all must be charged.
sources.assumptions: Interaction hierarchy/sparsity and predictive proxy quality.
sources.remaining_difference: A stronger direct learned-surrogate collision than additive-only controls. A graph CNP must beat a comparably queried proxy.
sources.code_status: Full paper read; author SPEX repository points to current shapiq integration. External ProxySPEX execution not implemented.

sources.name: Selective Explanations
sources.estimand: Reduce error to a target attribution method by selectively refining inaccurate amortized explanations.
sources.predictor_access: Predictor queries, amortized attribution and target explanation estimates.
sources.training_target: Learn explanation uncertainty/error, then refine selected explanations using an initial guess.
sources.learned_component: Selection/error model, with an amortized explainer.
sources.generalization: Across examples for the target explanation problem.
sources.inference_cost: Amortized inference plus extra Monte Carlo/regression work on selected examples.
sources.assumptions: Error labels/estimates and the same attribution estimand.
sources.remaining_difference: Detecting poor estimates and paying for refinement is already established. A stop/direct-evaluation option is a baseline requirement.
sources.code_status: Full paper read. Pinned author repository contains only README saying code is forthcoming; implementation unavailable.

sources.name: REX
sources.estimand: Reject predictions whose explanations have inadequate assessed quality.
sources.predictor_access: Predictor/explanations and machine- and human-side quality labels.
sources.explainer_inputs: Features used to estimate explanation quality; attribution judgments.
sources.generalization: Across examples evaluated in the quality-label setting.
sources.assumptions: Quality labels reflect the desired criterion; user acceptance is distinct from response fidelity.
sources.remaining_difference: Rejection alone is not a novel graph-edit response operator or an accuracy certificate.
sources.code_status: Full current paper read. No verified author implementation located in the bounded search.

sources.name: GNN explanations that do not explain
sources.estimand: Detect degenerate self-explainable GNN subgraphs, including through Extension Sufficiency Test.
sources.predictor_access: Subgraph explanations and predictor behavior under relevant graph extensions.
sources.explainer_inputs: Original graph, explanation and extension/perturbation family.
sources.training_target: Analysis/evaluation rather than the proposed response-regression target.
sources.learned_component: The evaluated self-explainable models; EST is an evaluation procedure.
sources.inference_cost: Additional predictor evaluations over extensions; empirical checks are not a universal proof.
sources.assumptions: Applicable extension semantics. An explanation may encode a label without identifying its basis.
sources.remaining_difference: Use the stress test on native subgraph methods. For response surrogates use matched transcripts, removed/shuffled responses and held-out functions.
sources.code_status: Pinned GOOD/kernel/pipelines/xai_metric_utils.py and full paper inspected.

sources.name: GFlowExplainer
sources.predictor_access: Target GNN predictions for explanatory rewards.
sources.explainer_inputs: Current subgraph state and graph context.
sources.training_target: GFlowNet flow consistency with terminal explanation reward.
sources.generalization: Across graph instances of the explanation setting.
sources.inference_cost: Sequential graph construction, action scoring and reward queries.
sources.assumptions: State/action DAG, chosen reward and legal subgraph transitions; no general chemical-validity guarantee.
sources.remaining_difference: Learning an explanation distribution is known. Signed edit-response regression has a different target but still uses a known conditioning operator.
sources.code_status: Full primary paper read. An author implementation was not verified; links in its baseline section are not its own code.

sources.name: ICExplainer
sources.estimand: Small graph perturbations that change a frozen GNN prediction while retaining distributional consistency.
sources.predictor_access: Paper describes black-box GNN outputs; prediction loss uses changed-graph probabilities.
sources.explainer_inputs: Noisy graph, variational semantic latent and diffusion timestep.
sources.training_target: Variational graph reconstruction, diffusion distribution loss and prediction-flip loss.
sources.learned_component: Graph distribution encoder and PPGN-based denoising generator.
sources.inference_cost: Diffusion steps, sampling and target-model evaluations.
sources.assumptions: Learned graph distribution and prediction loss do not themselves prove arbitrary molecular transformations valid.
sources.remaining_difference: Valid counterfactual generation already has direct predecessors; it is distinct from accurately reconstructing every signed action response.
sources.code_status: Primary nine-page PDF read through publisher reader; local PDF request failed. No verified author code located.

sources.name: Conditional neural processes
sources.estimand: Conditional predictions of unobserved function values from observed input-output pairs.
sources.predictor_access: Function samples; no need for predictor parameters.
sources.explainer_inputs: Context set of pairs and target inputs.
sources.training_target: Held-out target predictive likelihood over sampled functions.
sources.learned_component: Pair encoder, symmetric aggregation and decoder.
sources.generalization: New functions after observing a small context set.
sources.inference_cost: Context encoding plus target decoding; linear context aggregation in the basic CNP.
sources.assumptions: Training function distribution, finite representation bottleneck and generalization.
sources.remaining_difference: This is the proposed operator: replace x by a graph-edit embedding and center its output at identity. The response-only implementation is exactly the matched CNP class.
sources.code_status: Full paper and pinned original deterministic encoder/decoder notebook code inspected.

sources.name: Conditional graph neural processes
sources.estimand: Conditional function reconstruction on irregular domains using graph relations.
sources.predictor_access: Context samples, not a special frozen-model identity.
sources.explainer_inputs: Input-output samples and a graph/metric relationship.
sources.generalization: Families of functions with relational structure.
sources.assumptions: Chosen graph geometry captures relevant relations.
sources.remaining_difference: Adding a graph encoder to function conditioning is established; an edit-specific input representation alone does not escape this precedent.
sources.code_status: Full primary paper read; no verified author code located.

sources.name: Message Passing Neural Processes
sources.estimand: Predictions of partially observed structured stochastic processes.
sources.predictor_access: Relational data and observed context labels.
sources.explainer_inputs: Graph, sparse labels and query nodes.
sources.learned_component: Message passing and a global latent process representation.
sources.generalization: Disjoint processes and few-shot tasks in evaluated settings.
sources.assumptions: Relational locality and a suitable process distribution.
sources.remaining_difference: Structured few-shot process learning predates this proposal. The graph-edit problem remains a task specialization.
sources.code_status: Full primary paper read; author-specific runnable code not verified.

sources.name: Deep Adaptive Design
sources.estimand: Sequential Bayesian experimental design maximizing expected information gain.
sources.predictor_access: A differentiable generative likelihood/simulator and parameter prior.
sources.generalization: Repeated experiments from the specified model/prior.

sources.estimand: Sequential experiments supporting downstream decision utility.

sources.estimand: Domain-specific local sequence surrogates, including epistatic and nonlinear response structure.
